   Trump ordered to sit for deposition in his US$10 billion BBC lawsuit, AP reports
 Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox
 US President Donald Trump is suing Britain’s publicly funded broadcaster for defamation over a speech clip that was misleadingly edited.
 PHOTO: EPA
 Published   Oct 23, 2026, 12:41 AM
 Updated   Oct 23, 2026, 06:55 AM
 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise A federal judge ordered Donald Trump to sit for a deposition by 11 December in his US$10 billion BBC defamation case, after the BBC said he was stalling.
 Trump says the BBC misled viewers by splicing his 6 January 2021 speech, while the BBC admitted the edits were misleading and apologised, but denied defamation.
 The BBC is seeking financial records from Mar-a-Lago and Trump-linked firms, as the case follows a Panorama bias row that caused resignations and public backlash.
 AI generated
 MIAMI - A federal judge on Oct 22 ordered Donald Trump to sit for a deposition by Dec 11 in his US$10 billion (S$12.7 billion) defamation lawsuit against the BBC, which has accused the US president of stalling to avoid answering questions under oath, the Associated Press reported.
 Trump is suing Britain’s publicly funded broadcaster for at least US$10 billion over a misleadingly edited clip of a speech. 
 The case is one of several Trump has privately filed against the news media as part of wider pressure campaign against coverage he dislikes.
 US Magistrate Judge Enjolique Lett ordered Trump to take questions from the BBC’s lawyers under oath in a ruling from the bench at a court hearing on Oct 22, according to a spokesman for Trump’s personal legal team.
 Trump cancelled a deposition in October, citing conflicts with his presidential duties.
 The Trump spokesman said the lawsuit is aimed at holding the BBC accountable for defamation and “reckless election interference.”
 The BBC declined to comment. It previously admitted the edits were misleading and apologised to Trump, though it denies being liable for defamation.
 Trump’s lawsuit filed in December in Florida federal court accuses the BBC of intentionally misleading viewers into thinking he directed supporters to storm the US Capitol by splicing together different parts of a Jan 6, 2021 speech.
 In court filings, the broadcaster has accused Trump and his lawyers of dragging their feet in response to their requests for records and other information that is exchanged between parties in a process known as discovery.
 The BBC is seeking financial records from Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club and the web of business entities associated with him, saying the information is necessary to defend against Trump’s damages claims.
 Trump’s lawyers say the requests are too broad and irrelevant to the case. They have also denied in court filings that Trump is avoiding a deposition, saying Trump’s duties and security needs must take precedence.
 The edited speech appeared in a BBC Panorama documentary show shortly before the 2024 presidential election, which Trump won.
 A leaked internal BBC memo cited the edits as evidence of potential political bias, sparking a public relations crisis for the broadcaster and leading to high-level resignations. REUTERS
